clue.text: Give grade incorrectly — much troubled in consequence

indicators.note: giving something incorrectly means getting it wrong, so the letters of the two words before are set out wrongly

explanation.surface: A teacher marks a paper wrongly and the pupil is upset as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorrectly' rearranges GIVEGRADE; 'in consequence' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be aggrieved is to feel resentful and greatly wronged, i.e. sorely upset.

clue.text: Punishing the undergraduate making a joke about money

indicators.note: the joke goes around, about, the word for money, which sits inside it

parts.note: a gag is a joke
tin is an old slang word for money

explanation.surface: A student is disciplined for a quip about cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. Gating, in Oxford and Cambridge colleges, confines a student to college as a punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Gating is the college penalty of confining a student to the premises after hours.

clue.text: Concerned with the first lady's stewards

parts.note: re means concerning or with regard to
Eve, the first woman in Genesis, with her possessive

explanation.surface: Something to do with the First Lady's household staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The first lady' looks like a president's wife; here it is Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a manorial official or steward managing an estate.

clue.text: Call for more character and heart to be shown

parts.note: an en is a printing measure, treated here as a character of type
the core is the heart of something

explanation.surface: Someone asks for personality and feeling to be displayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be shown' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An encore is an audience's shouted request for a further performance.

clue.text: Picked men with guns for a Greek heroine

parts.note: elect means chosen or picked
RA, the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners

explanation.surface: Armed men are selected for a heroine from Greek legend.
explanation.walkthrough: RA is the Royal Artillery, the regiment of British army gunners.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra is the daughter of Agamemnon in Greek tragedy who avenges her father.

clue.text: Remember mounting hesitation over form of prayer

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means going upwards, so the hesitation word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: er is a sound of hesitation
a collect is a short prayer of the Anglican and Catholic liturgy

explanation.surface: Recall growing reluctance about a style of praying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' turns ER into RE in this down clue; 'over' puts it above COLLECT.
explanation.definitionFit: To recollect is to call something back to mind.

clue.text: Poor lot if employed in a minister's office

indicators.note: employed means put to use, so the letters of the three words are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: A deprived group finds work in a government department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employed' rearranges POORLOTIF.
explanation.definitionFit: A government minister's portfolio is the department or responsibility the post holds.

clue.text: A number viewed outside sporting contest

indicators.note: the word for viewed is placed outside, around, the word for a contest

parts.note: seen means viewed
an event is a contest in a sports meeting

explanation.surface: A crowd figure watched at a sports meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' splits the word for viewed around the contest word, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Seventeen is a whole number, one more than sixteen.

clue.text: Go and apply for one

parts.note: to beg is to ask or plead for something
taken as written

explanation.surface: Head off and put in a request for a single item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Begone!' is an old imperative ordering someone away.

clue.text: A cause of increasing litter

explanation.surface: Something that causes a litter of animals to grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'litter' suggests a brood of puppies; here it is a portable bed for carrying the injured.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that stretches things lengthens them, and a stretcher is also a portable carrying bed.

clue.text: The kind that is offensive

parts.note: a sort is a kind or type
i.e., from Latin id est, means that is

explanation.surface: The type of person who is rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' is a noun here, a military attack, not the adjective 'rude'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sortie is a sudden sally by troops, an attack or offensive.

clue.text: Arrange a merger and get it near settlement

indicators.note: a settlement is an arrangement, so the letters of these three words are settled into a new order

explanation.surface: Fix up a company combination and get close to a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settlement' rearranges GETITNEAR; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To integrate is to combine parts into a whole, as two firms combine.

clue.text: Not quite all losing money — the majority though

indicators.note: the word all loses the letter standing for money

parts.note: taken as written
L stands for the pound, from Latin libra
most means the greater part

explanation.surface: Not entirely everyone loses cash, though most do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' drops one L, the pound sign, from ALL; 'though' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Almost means nearly, falling just short of the whole.

clue.text: A food store takes time in organizing display

indicators.note: the store takes in, holds, the word for time

parts.note: a pantry is a larder for food
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A larder takes ages to organise a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' is the container signal, the time word going in after the first letter; 'A' and 'in organizing' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Pageantry is splendid ceremonial show and spectacle.

clue.text: Most foreign streets are out of line

indicators.note: the street abbreviations stand outside the word for line, which sits inside them

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, plural here so two of them
a range is a line, as in a mountain range

explanation.surface: The oddest roads are not aligned properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'streets' gives two STs, and 'out of' puts them either side of RANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Strangest means most alien or unfamiliar.

clue.text: Make sure disputes can't arise

indicators.note: disputes means challenges or argues over, so the letters of the two words are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Ensure that no quarrels can come up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disputes' rearranges CANTARISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain is to find out for certain.

clue.text: German agreement many block

parts.note: ja is German for yes
M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, is a crossword sense of many

explanation.surface: A German treaty is obstructed by many.
explanation.walkthrough: M as 'many' comes from the Roman numeral for a thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: To jam is to obstruct or stop something up.

clue.text: Black stream

explanation.definitionFit: Jet is a deep glossy black, and a jet is a forceful stream of liquid or gas.

clue.text: A set piece for the board?

definitions.text: A set piece for the board?

parts.words: A set piece for the board?
parts.note: a set piece suggests a planned move in football, but here it is one of the pieces in a chess set used on the board

explanation.surface: A pre-planned move for the company directors.
explanation.definitionFit: Each chess or draughts piece is called a man.

clue.text: The person painting European entertainer

parts.note: an artist is someone who paints

explanation.surface: A painter from Europe who performs on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional performer such as a singer or dancer.

clue.text: A penman getting credit

parts.note: a scribe writes by hand, a penman

explanation.surface: A writer receives recognition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link; 'credit' is the verb, as in crediting a work to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascribe something to someone is to attribute it to them.

clue.text: Note nitrogen is one element

parts.note: ti (or te) is a note of the sol-fa scale
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen; the answer appearing backwards at the start of this word is a coincidence

explanation.surface: Observe that nitrogen is a chemical element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' is a sol-fa note, not 'take note'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tin is a metallic chemical element, symbol Sn.

clue.text: Check a little crawler carries small change

indicators.note: the crawler carries, holds inside it, the letter for a coin

parts.note: an insect is a small creeping creature
p, a penny, is the smallest British coin

explanation.surface: Examine a bug carrying a few coppers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries' puts P inside INSECT; p means penny in British money.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to examine closely.

clue.text: Put on a top-coat

parts.note: suggests dressing in an overcoat, but means applying a final glossy layer of paint

explanation.surface: Get dressed in an overcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: To enamel is to coat a surface with a hard glossy paint finish.

clue.text: With private transport always make speedy progress

parts.note: a car is one's own vehicle
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: Having your own car means you can always get along quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to rush along at high speed.

clue.text: Flowery letters for all maybe

indicators.note: maybe signals that the letters of the two words could be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: Ornate lettering for everyone perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges FORALL; 'letters' is a link telling you to use the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Floral means relating to or decorated with blooms.

clue.text: Exercising some self-restraint, Ernest shut up

indicators.note: some means a part of the following words, which hold the letters within them

explanation.surface: Ernest was showing some restraint, so he went quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes the run spanning 'restraint' and 'Ernest'; 'Exercising' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To intern is to confine or imprison, especially in wartime.

clue.text: He'll come down hard on a craft worker about to be sick

parts.note: SS, a steamship, is a craft
to ail is to be unwell
the worker ant is a crossword staple for worker

explanation.surface: A tradesman about to throw up will be severe on someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link: the worker is near the sickness, which comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An assailant is an attacker, one who launches a violent onslaught.

clue.text: When the outlook is dark things must change

indicators.note: the letters of the word before are required to alter their order

explanation.surface: In gloomy prospects, matters have to be altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must change' rearranges THINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Nights are the hours of darkness when the view outside is black.

clue.text: Practised play

parts.note: a theatrical piece that the cast has run through before opening, or play done for practice

explanation.surface: A drama the cast has run through.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehearsed means practised in preparation, as a play is before performance.

clue.text: This takes the biscuit in a social reformer!

parts.note: a rusk is a hard dry biscuit
taken as written

explanation.surface: This beats everything, in someone who reforms society!
explanation.walkthrough: John Ruskin was a Victorian critic and social thinker. 'This takes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: John Ruskin, Victorian critic, campaigned for social and economic reform.

clue.text: Short in support, and that's astounding

indicators.note: the word for short goes in the word for support

parts.note: a sling supports an injured arm
tart means sharp or curt, as a short answer is

explanation.surface: Lacking in backing, which is surprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'and' is a link. 'Short' as in a short, sharp reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Startling means very surprising or amazing.
